reviews.review: Still recommended to play for a different experience than it's sequel. This one is 2D

One of my favorite roguelikes, Risk of Rain is an amazing game. This is a game that requires some skill and learning to get good at, but once you do, it feels amazing. The possible playable characters are all fun in their own ways, without one dominating the meta, the unlocked items are fun and can be combined in fun ways.

Overall, one of my favorite games. Would recommend.
One of the best games and best roguelikes I have ever played. Would die again.

I am not one who normally plays roguelike games, as I hate starting from the beginning, but something about Risk of Rain keeps me invested. Challenges are layered throughout, and upon completing those challenges, more items and survivors become available, making every playthrough a completely unique experience. I realize that describes most games of the genre, so let me break things down:

First off, the story is that you are alone on a mysterious planet trying to survive, and everything about the game reflects that. The music is mysterious and creepy, yet still brings feelings of peace or badassitude depending on the track. The weirdness of the items matches, and each one is vastly different from the others.

Every character has a completely different feel to them, and you can either find your favorite or try to get good with them all. Most are ranged, but there are a handful of melee survivors if you want to go head to head with the creatures of the planet.

Finally, the artifacts. These relics are scattered around each map, and drastically change the game - with glass (decreased health, increased damage), command (choose which item you want when you pick one up), honor (only elite enemies spawn), and more, you can customize your experience to be as easy or hard as you want. Whether you wanna decimate everything in front of you, or survive by the skin of your teeth, both can be accomplished depending on the settings for the run.

And now that Risk of Rain 2 is out, I would absolutely recommend it. The transition from 2d to 3d is way better than I ever expected.
